holding_summary: A traveler who checked baggage with a hotel's authorized clerk the evening before registering, and who registered and became a guest the next day, was entitled to recover for baggage lost while it remained in the hotel's custody; the court treated the guest relationship as established once he registered and put the burden on the hotel to disprove liability.

quotes.text: His evidence shows that he registered at the hotel about twelve o’clock during the day of the 23d, and at that time became a guest.

If we concede that the appellant is correct in its conclusion that the appellee did not become a guest when he deposited his baggage at the hotel on the evening of the 22d, still, the verdict and judgment of the court below can be justified upon the ground that his baggage was in the custody of the hotel when he actually became a guest; that is, in custody of that servant of the hotel who was charged with the duty of receiving and keeping safely the baggage of guests.
And if circumstances existed that would relieve it from liability, the burden would be upon the appellant to establish that fact, and it was not done in this case.
